intended_object: The subgroup Ô^× = ∏_v 𝒪_v^× of the finite idele group (𝔸_K^f)^× of a Dedekind domain R with fraction field K. It consists of the finite ideles whose component at every height-one prime v is a unit of the local ring of integers 𝒪_v. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The carrier is the set of units x of 𝔸ᶠ[R, K] such that Valued.v (x_v) = 1 at every height-one prime v. In the completion K_v, an element has valuation exactly 1 if and only if it lies in 𝒪_v^×. So the condition says each component of x is a local unit. That is exactly ∏_v 𝒪_v^× embedded in the ideles. Every such family is automatically a unit of the finite adele ring: it is integral everywhere and so is its inverse.

The closure proofs are standard. Multiplicativity of the valuation gives closure under products, and `valued_coe_units_inv_apply` gives closure under inverses.

The library proves `integralUnits_eq_units_integralAdeles` (the subgroup equals the unit group of the integral finite adeles) and `ker_toFractionalIdeal` (it is the kernel of the map to invertible fractional ideals). Both match the textbook role of Ô^×.

The setting, a Dedekind domain with its fraction field, is the natural one, and it matches Mathlib's own `FiniteAdeleRing`. I found no Mathlib declaration that defines this subgroup.
